correctness.rationale: Independently used all primitive residue pairs (24 for modulus 6 and 48 for modulus 8), not projective states. The two digit maps send the root pair (0,1) through all Stern pairs with indices 0≤n<2^r after r steps, including leading zero digits. Exact characteristic polynomials and the induced Cayley–Hamilton recurrences give both dyadic prefix generating functions. Their difference cancels to 2z⁵(1−z)/L(z), and each prefix series has coefficient 1/12 at the simple 1/(1−2z) term. The reduced difference has simple poles: −1 and ten distinct nonreal poles of modulus 1/√2, none cancelled by the numerator. After normalization, partial fractions give a finite sum of distinct unit-frequency exponentials with nonzero coefficients and an exponentially decaying error. Its limiting Cesàro mean is zero and its mean square is strictly positive. If either sign had no excursion bounded away from zero arbitrarily late, the corresponding positive or negative part would have vanishing Cesàro mean; the zero mean then forces both parts to vanish on average, contradicting the positive mean square by boundedness. This checks the all-index identity and both strict limits.
residual_risks: No exact limsup or liminf constant is claimed.
